file_roles.evidence: ha_sequence::external_lock recorded the lock on the underlying handler unconditionally, 'file->m_lock_type= lock_type;', directly below a comment saying it exists to 'satisfy DBUG_ASSERT checks in ha_* functions in handler.cc'. It becomes 'if (!error) file->m_lock_type= lock_type;'. The commit states the same thing: 'The bug was the we copied the lock type to the underlying engine even when external_lock failed.'

rationale: The assertion is 'sql/handler.h:3011: virtual handler::~handler(): Assertion `m_lock_type == 2' failed', so the handler was recorded as locked when it was destroyed, and handler.h is not in the gold set. The field was written during the failed INSERT, which the test expects to fail with ER_BINLOG_STMT_MODE_AND_ROW_ENGINE, and the assertion fires much later during DROP SEQUENCE. Two different statements, which is why no frame in the crashing stack reaches the code that was wrong.
notes: The gold file does appear in the stack, at 'ha_sequence::~ha_sequence ... sql/ha_sequence.cc:62', but that is the destructor and the fix is in external_lock. Right file, wrong function, which is now the fourth instance of that shape after KAFKA-3123, KAFKA-9743 and MDEV-17725, and the cause is the same each time: the call that wrote the bad state had already returned. The reporter also notes 'No visible effect on a non-debug build', so outside a debug server this defect produces no symptom at all and nothing to localize from.
